claims_disputed.claim: Taxonomy of 11 categories / 27 subcategories / 73 leaf types from 833 fault threads.
claims_disputed.reason: §4.6: kappa 0.938 was measured only in Round 5, after the same two coders had jointly built and reconciled the codebook over four rounds; there was no independent third coder. 'No new structural categories emerged' comes from reclassifying already-coded threads, not an incremental saturation analysis. §5 exemplars also include projects that are not MCP servers (apache/apisix logging plugin, cherry-studio client, langgraphjs stream.stop, browser-use timeouts, openinference tracing), and 'Model Provider Integration' is a host/client concern, so the 'MCP server runtime fault' boundary is blurred.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: This is a descriptive fault taxonomy of MCP-related repositories, with no comparison against another integration approach and no measurement of agent outcomes. Nothing in it is positive evidence for MCP as an integration layer, so 'mixed' implies a balance that is absent.

missed_issues: A second internal inconsistency: §6 'Risk-based prioritization' cites Schema Compatibility practitioner confirmation as 69%, but Table 1 gives 58%. State & Configuration is reported as both 17.1% and 17.2% of 833.
Table 1 Yes% values average 43.5%, i.e. ~11.7 of 27 subcategories per respondent. This confirms the abstract's '20 of 27' cannot come from Table 1 as presented.
Survey items are yes/no recognition prompts with no distractor/control items, so a ≥25% recognition floor cannot discriminate real fault classes from plausible-sounding ones (acquiescence bias).

Corpus scope creep: 'MCP server' repositories include gateways, clients, tracing libraries and agent frameworks (§5 exemplars), so some categories (Model Provider Integration, Configuration Handling via apisix) may not be MCP-server faults.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and with marking the abstract's survey claim unsupported. I downgrade the taxonomy-construction claim from strong to moderate because kappa was measured after joint consensus rounds and the corpus scope is blurred. P04 should be neutral: this is a fault catalogue, not evidence for or against MCP.
